title: Invariance-Induced Borrow Checker Block
pattern: Forcing a covariant type (like a shared reference or lifetime) into an invariant context (like mutable references `&mut T` or `Cell<T>`) under a single generic lifetime parameter.
why_bad: It prevents the compiler from performing lifetime coercion (shortening a lifetime), because invariance requires that the type parameter must be exactly identical. This causes the borrow checker to reject perfectly safe code.
detection: A struct containing nested references within a mutable reference or cell that uses a single unified lifetime parameter.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Invariance is essential for memory safety when mutability is present (to prevent writing a short-lived reference into a long-lived container).
fix: Avoid collapsing distinct lifetimes inside mutable references; use multiple lifetime parameters when nesting references under mutability.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021), Chapter 2 ("Foundations - Borrowing and Lifetimes - Lifetime Variance"), pp. 536-541.
